claims.statement: The repo's test matrix is: all TypeScript packages use Vitest with co-located `*.test.ts` unit tests run in the Node environment (github-bot is the exception, keeping tests in a separate `test/` directory), while the Python planes (modal-infra, sandbox-runtime) use pytest suites under `tests/test_*.py` with pytest-asyncio in auto mode; the root `vitest.workspace.ts` joins all per-package Vitest configs.

Per-package test entry points are `npm test -w <pkg>` for TypeScript units, `npm run test:integration -w @open-inspect/control-plane` for the workerd integration suite, and `pytest tests/ -v` run from inside `packages/modal-infra` or `packages/sandbox-runtime` for Python; Python formatting is `ruff check --fix && ruff format` from the package directory.

Control-plane integration tests (`test/integration/**/*.test.ts`) execute inside a real workerd runtime via the `cloudflareTest()` plugin of `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers`, configured in `vitest.integration.config.ts` against the test-only `wrangler.jsonc` bindings (SESSION Durable Object with SQLite migration, D1, KV, R2).

The integration suite automatically applies the production D1 schema: `readD1Migrations` parses `terraform/d1/migrations/` (the same directory Terraform applies in production) and injects it as a `TEST_MIGRATIONS` binding, and the global setup file `test/integration/apply-migrations.ts` calls `applyD1Migrations(env.DB, env.TEST_MIGRATIONS)` before tests run; migration-behavior tests replay individual migrations from that binding against hand-restored pre-migration schemas.

The workers pool isolates D1 storage per test file, so integration test files run in parallel without interference; within a file all tests share one D1 instance and must call `cleanD1Tables()` from `test/integration/cleanup.ts` in `beforeEach`/`afterEach` — it issues a single `DELETE FROM …` across every table in the schema to prevent cross-test pollution.

The integration helpers (`test/integration/helpers.ts`) give tests production-shaped fixtures: `initSession()`/`initNamedSession()` write a D1 session-index row through `SessionIndexStore` and then POST `/internal/init` to the real SESSION Durable Object; `queryDO()` executes raw SQL inside the DO via `runInSessionDO` (the `runInDurableObject` seam in `session-do-access.ts`, the one place the stub is typed as `SessionDO`); `seedEvents()`/`seedMessage()` insert rows directly into DO SQLite with a monotonically increasing `timeline_sequence`; `openClientWs()` upgrades through `SELF.fetch` and optionally completes the WS-token subscribe flow with `collectMessages` (which must start before the triggering send).

`serviceFetch()` in the integration helpers sends requests with production-equivalent credentials: it signs each request with the shared sig1 scheme (`buildServiceAuthHeaders` against per-service `SERVICE_AUTH_SECRET_*` bindings) and, for `service: "web"`, additionally seeds a real Better Auth user/identity/session into D1 and attaches the HMAC-signed browser session cookie — so browser-owned route tests exercise the same compound credential as production.

The integration harness pins runtime parity and a hermetic outbound world: Miniflare is pinned to `compatibilityDate: "2024-09-23"` with `nodejs_compat` to match the Terraform-managed production runtime; `luxon` is aliased to its CommonJS build because vite 8's ESM resolution breaks cron-parser under the workers pool (the scheduler would silently skip overdue automations); `outboundService` returns 404 for `*.modal.run`, deterministic fixtures for the OpenAI and xAI device-flow/token endpoints, and throws on any unexpected outbound request; and a `onUnhandledError` filter tolerates Better Auth's internal APIError rejections.

In CI the control-plane integration job is sharded 2× (`--shard=1/2`, `--shard=2/2`, `fail-fast: false`) with a 10-minute timeout, and `packages/control-plane/Dockerfile.test` packages the same `npm run test:integration` command into a self-contained `node:22-slim` image that pre-builds `@open-inspect/shared` and copies the D1 migrations, so the suite can run outside a checked-out workspace.

Control-plane typechecking runs three separate tsc programs: the production `tsconfig.json` (no Node globals), `tsconfig.test.json` (adds Node types because co-located unit tests use `node:crypto`/`node:fs`/`import.meta.url`), and `test/integration/tsconfig.json`, which compiles against `@cloudflare/workers-types` plus the `cloudflare:test` module and merges the test `env` with the production `Env` via `env.d.ts`.

`packages/shared/src/module-boundaries.test.ts` is an architecture-pinning test that parses every production module of `@open-inspect/shared` with the TypeScript AST and asserts implementation modules never import the package-root or shared-types barrels (including via `@open-inspect/shared` self-imports) and that the internal dependency graph has no runtime cycles and no compile-time cycles, with type-only edges classified separately. Agents must not weaken it to make an import that crosses these boundaries pass.

`packages/shared/src/types/boundary-schemas.test.ts` pins the Zod schemas guarding every client/server boundary (`createSessionRequestSchema`, `clientMessageSchema`, `serverMessageSchema`, `sendPromptRequestSchema`, `sandboxEventSchema`, the Linear callback schemas, the automation repository schemas, and more) with both valid and malformed payloads — valid payloads must parse and partial/empty-string/type-confused payloads must be rejected — because these schemas are the wire contract the web client, bots, and sandbox runtime agree on.

`packages/shared/src/types/type-contracts.test.ts` uses `expectTypeOf` to pin the compile-time relationship between the public Zod schemas and the hand-written TypeScript types (e.g. `CreateSessionRequest` must equal `z.output<typeof createSessionRequestSchema>`, `RepositoryInput` must equal `z.input<typeof repositoryInputSchema>`), including the repository transform boundary where normalization makes the output type stricter than the input.

The web package's `client-auth-boundary-eslint.test.ts` and `server-auth-boundary-eslint.test.ts` run the real repository ESLint flat config against synthetic files to pin the auth boundaries: client code cannot import `next-auth`, raw `fetch` is banned everywhere except the two app-owned transports (`browser-api-fetch.ts`, `control-plane-transport.ts`), and server routes must use `getServerAuthSession` from `@/lib/server-auth-session` instead of importing `@/lib/auth` or the framework directly — proving the `eslint.config.js` rules stay armed.

`packages/control-plane/src/router.policy.test.ts` pins the route policy table: every route must declare `authentication` metadata and `supportedScmProviders`; representative routes are pinned per auth kind (`public`, `handler-authenticated`, `web-service`, `user`, `user-or-service`, `sandbox` with session-id extraction, `user-or-service-with-sandbox-fallback`); diff authentication is method-specific; management/broker routes are non-cacheable; and `scm-credentials` is the only GitLab-specific SCM exception. The kinds come from the `RouteAuthentication` union in `src/routes/shared.ts`.

The control-plane package carries architecture-enforcing ESLint bans (enforced by CI lint rather than a Vitest file): `.DB` member access is forbidden outside the composition roots, each of which (`src/index.ts`, `src/session/durable-object.ts`, `src/router.ts`, the queue consumer) carries a single justified inline `eslint-disable`; the session composition root (`session/components.ts`) may only be imported by the platform adapter (`session/durable-object.ts`), which only the worker entrypoint may import; and repo-wide `no-restricted-imports` forces auth-owned and service-auth-owned names to be imported from `@open-inspect/shared/auth` and `@open-inspect/shared/service-auth`.

Cross-plane contract tests keep the TypeScript and Python sides numerically identical: `packages/modal-infra/tests/test_build_sandbox_lifecycle.py` regex-reads `packages/shared/src/types/integrations.ts` and `packages/control-plane/src/image-builds/timeouts.ts` to pin Modal's build-timeout constants and finalization-grace mirror, and both that file and `packages/control-plane/src/sandbox/sandbox-env.test.ts` pin the image-build callback env keys and reserved-key scrub lists to the shared manifest `packages/sandbox-runtime/src/sandbox_runtime/image_build_callback_env.json`.

Because the Python contract tests read TypeScript sources by path, the Python CI workflow's trigger paths explicitly include `packages/control-plane/src/image-builds/timeouts.ts` and `packages/shared/src/types/integrations.ts`, so changing those TypeScript constants re-runs the Python suites.

`packages/sandbox-runtime/tests/test_bridge_push.py` pins the bridge's git-push semantics that security and correctness depend on: stderr redaction of embedded tokens in push errors, the terminate-then-kill timeout ladder with its exact `wait_for` timeout values, and manifest-targeted multi-repo pushing (case-insensitive identity matching against the repo manifest, canonical checkout path selection, and no filesystem access for identities not in the manifest).

`packages/shared/src/service-auth.test.ts` verifies the sig1 service-signing scheme against committed golden vectors in `packages/shared/test-fixtures/service-auth-vectors.json` (canonical request string, body hash, signature hex, header shape, malformed-header rejections), making the shared auth primitive resistant to casual re-derivation.

`packages/control-plane/src/worker-build.test.ts` builds the actual control-plane bundle and asserts it uses workerd's `node:async_hooks` implementation (no `AsyncLocalStorage` polyfill) and the ESM build of OpenTelemetry semantic conventions — a build-output pin, not a unit test of source.

The integration suite's `session-do-collaborator-wiring.test.ts` pins SessionDO collaborator edges that have success-shaped fallbacks (warm-on-typing spawn, snapshot trigger, branch-push wiring) and are otherwise invisible to the rest of the suite, reaching past DO encapsulation through a single confined seam (`componentsOf` in `session-do-access.ts`).

Unit-level router tests (`src/router.*.test.ts`) complement the integration suite with a Node-environment harness: `router.test-support.ts` provides `signedServiceRequest()`, which signs each request individually with `buildServiceAuthHeaders` (sig1 binds method, URL, and body, so no reusable header exists) against `TEST_SERVICE_SECRETS`, plus a shared `TEST_BACKGROUND_TASK_CONTEXT` double for the `BackgroundTasks` seam.

`packages/sandbox-runtime/tests/conftest.py` installs an autouse fixture redirecting the runtime's fixed file paths (repo manifest, boot warnings, tunnel env) to per-test `tmp_path` locations, because this suite routinely executes inside a live Open-Inspect sandbox where the real `/tmp/oi-repo-manifest.json` belongs to the running session.

The sandbox-runtime suite additionally contains plain `node --test` files (`tests/*.test.mjs`) for the sandbox's injected JavaScript tools, run in CI via `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` with Node 22 installed in the Python job — these tools are not pytest-covered.

The modal-infra suite pins the data-plane HTTP API's validation and failure contract by driving the FastAPI route functions directly: string booleans and invalid typed fields are rejected with HTTP 400, missing/empty `control_plane_url`/`sandbox_auth_token` return 400 with the field named, unknown fields are forwarded to the session-config helper, and generic manager failures surface as HTTP 500 with the request logged but details not leaked.

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs on push/PR to `main` with path filters and comprises: lint & format (ESLint, complexity-reporter test, Prettier check, Knip), typecheck, a web production build, control-plane unit tests (shared then control-plane), the sharded workerd integration job, web tests, and all three bot test suites — every job that compiles or tests dependent packages builds `@open-inspect/shared` first because worker packages import its built `dist/` output.

`npm run lint:complexity` (`scripts/lint-complexity.mjs`) runs ESLint with `complexity: ["warn", { max: 0, variant: "classic" }]` over `packages/**/*.{ts,tsx}` to collect every function's cyclomatic complexity and print a distribution plus a hotspot table (production functions over 20, top 25). It is deliberately report-only — findings never affect the exit code, and test files are excluded from the production hotspot table; its diagnostic-message parser has its own `node --test` suite (`npm run test:lint-complexity`, which is what CI runs) so an ESLint diagnostic-shape change fails loudly.

Knip detects unused exports, files, and dependencies using per-workspace entries in `knip.json` (which declares integration tests and the sandbox runtime's injected `.js` tools as entry points so they are not flagged); CI runs it with `--no-exit-code`, so findings are advisory review items rather than failures to suppress.

The husky pre-commit hook runs lint-staged, which applies `eslint --fix` + `prettier --write` to `*.{ts,tsx}`, `prettier --write` to `*.{js,jsx,json,md,yaml,yml,css}`, and `ruff check --fix` + `ruff format` to Python under the provider-infra packages; the hook activates the modal-infra venv first when present so `ruff` is on PATH.
Commit messages are expected to follow conventional commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`, `test:`) with subjects under 72 characters, details in the PR body.

Every Vitest package exposes `test:coverage` using the v8 provider with `text` + `json` reporters over production sources (excluding test files, `.d.ts`, and the worker entrypoint), but coverage is not a CI gate.
